statement: No CFC rule was found that attributes the undistributed profits of a foreign subsidiary to a Thai company shareholder. The official corporate-income-tax overview taxes a juristic company or partnership on its own Thai business or Thai-derived income; checked the Revenue Code corporate-income-tax and international-tax materials.
quote: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) is a direct tax levied on a juristic company or partnership carrying on business in Thailand or not carrying on business in Thailand but deriving certain types of income from Thailand.

subject: individual

The official personal-income-tax overview taxes a resident on Thai-source income and foreign-source income brought into Thailand; checked the Revenue Code personal-income-tax and international-tax materials.
quote: A resident of Thailand is liable to pay tax on income from sources in Thailand as well as on the portion of income from foreign sources that is brought into Thailand.

subject: individual
statement: No individual anti-abuse rule relevant to dividend receipt was found in the Revenue Department materials checked. The official anti-avoidance material addresses manipulated transfer pricing within MNEs and the company or juristic-partnership corporate-income-tax calculation; it is not extended here to an individual recipient.
quote: In order to prevent the evasion of taxation caused by manipulated transfer pricing within the MNEs, tax authorities can price goods and services by applying the provisions of Section 65 bis (4) (7), Section 65 ter, and Section 70 ter under the Revenue Code, Double Tax Agreements between Thailand and other countries, as well as Standard Accounting No. 37 and 47.

statement: No Indian CFC income-attribution regime was found in the current Income-tax Act 2025 materials. The Rules' CFC reference is solely a FATCA reporting definition for a sponsored controlled foreign corporation, not a rule attributing a foreign subsidiary's undistributed profits to an Indian shareholder. The official Act portal also confirms that the 2025 Act introduces no new tax.

statement: No CFC rules: the UAE Ministry of Finance states that the UAE corporate-tax regime does not include a controlled foreign company regime. This absence record applies to both company and individual CFC slots because those slots concern attribution of a foreign company's income under the UAE corporate-tax regime.
